es: Reconocer repetición, contraste, pregunta retórica y lenguaje emotivo en anuncios y eslóganes, y explicar el efecto de cada técnica sobre el público.

vocabulary.es: emotivo, que apela a los sentimientos

teaching.en: The slogan 'Clean rivers, clean streets, clean lives' relies on repetition: the same word returns three times, which makes the message memorable.
teaching.es: El eslogan «Ríos limpios, calles limpias, vidas limpias» se apoya en la repetición: la misma palabra vuelve tres veces, lo que hace el mensaje fácil de recordar.
teaching.explanationEs: Repetición: la misma palabra o estructura reaparece para que el eslogan se grabe.
segments: The slogan 'Clean rivers, clean streets, clean lives' relies on repetition:
the same word returns three times, which makes the message memorable.
teaching.audioText: The slogan 'Clean rivers, clean streets, clean lives' relies on repetition: the same word returns three times, which makes the message memorable.

teaching.en: An advert built on contrast sets two opposite ideas side by side, such as the slow old bus and the fast new one, to make the choice obvious.
teaching.es: Un anuncio construido sobre el contraste coloca dos ideas opuestas lado a lado, como el autobús viejo y lento y el nuevo y rápido, para que la elección resulte obvia.
teaching.explanationEs: Contraste: dos ideas opuestas en la misma frase o imagen destacan la opción que interesa.
segments: An advert built on contrast sets two opposite ideas side by side, such as
the slow old bus and the fast new one, to make the choice obvious.
teaching.audioText: An advert built on contrast sets two opposite ideas side by side, such as the slow old bus and the fast new one, to make the choice obvious.

teaching.en: A rhetorical question does not expect an answer, because the audience is meant to reach the obvious conclusion without being told.
teaching.es: Una pregunta retórica no espera respuesta, porque se pretende que el público llegue solo a la conclusión obvia sin que se la digan.
teaching.explanationEs: Pregunta retórica: se formula para pensar, no para recibir una respuesta.
segments: A rhetorical question does not expect an answer, because the audience
is meant to reach the obvious conclusion without being told.
teaching.audioText: A rhetorical question does not expect an answer, because the audience is meant to reach the obvious conclusion without being told.

teaching.en: Emotive language, such as shameful or heartbreaking, is another technique that persuades readers by appealing to feelings rather than facts.
teaching.es: El lenguaje emotivo, como «vergonzoso» o «desgarrador», es otra técnica que persuade a los lectores apelando a los sentimientos más que a los hechos.
teaching.explanationEs: Emotive = que apela a la emoción; suele sustituir datos por sentimientos.
segments: Emotive language, such as shameful or heartbreaking, is another technique
that persuades readers by appealing to feelings rather than facts.
teaching.audioText: Emotive language, such as shameful or heartbreaking, is another technique that persuades readers by appealing to feelings rather than facts.

teaching.en: Each technique has a different effect on the reader, so a good analysis names the technique first and then explains what it makes the audience feel.
teaching.es: Cada técnica tiene un efecto distinto en el lector, así que un buen análisis nombra primero la técnica y luego explica qué hace sentir al público.
teaching.explanationEs: Al analizar: primero la técnica y después su efecto (to + verbo).
segments: Each technique has a different effect on the reader, so a good analysis
names the technique first and then explains what it makes the audience feel.
teaching.audioText: Each technique has a different effect on the reader, so a good analysis names the technique first and then explains what it makes the audience feel.

teaching.en: Repetition helps to put emphasis on the central idea, which is why advertisers try to persuade us with short, memorable phrases.
teaching.es: La repetición ayuda a poner énfasis en la idea central, y por eso los publicistas intentan persuadirnos con frases breves y fáciles de recordar.
teaching.explanationEs: Put emphasis on + nombre: destacar una idea; emphasis es incontable.
segments: Repetition helps to put emphasis on the central idea, which is
why advertisers try to persuade us with short, memorable phrases.
teaching.audioText: Repetition helps to put emphasis on the central idea, which is why advertisers try to persuade us with short, memorable phrases.

prompt.es: Identifica la técnica principal del eslogan de la escuela de idiomas.

choices.text: It repeats the same word at the end of each short sentence.
It sets two opposite ideas side by side to show a choice.
It asks the reader a question that has an obvious answer.

feedback.es: More cierra cada frase corta: es repetición, no contraste ni pregunta retórica.

hint.es: Fíjate en la palabra que vuelve a aparecer en cada frase.

origin.text: A language school has put this slogan on every poster in the underground: Read more. Learn more. Be more.

prompt.es: Completa: «El anuncio usa el contraste para mostrar la diferencia.»

answer.text: contrast
accepted: contrast

feedback.es: El contraste enfrenta dos ideas opuestas (lento y ruidoso frente a rápido y silencioso); en inglés se llama contrast.

hint.es: Se parece mucho a la palabra española.

origin.text: The advert compares the old bus with the new one: the first is slow and noisy, the second is fast and silent. It uses ___ to show the difference.

prompt.es: Ordena: «El eslogan usa la repetición para hacerlo memorable.»

answer.text: The slogan uses repetition to make it memorable

feedback.es: Se nombra la técnica y el efecto va al final con to + verbo.

hint.es: Primero la técnica; al final, to + efecto.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada eslogan con su técnica.

pairs: Clean town, clean park, clean home.
Old cars are noisy. New cars are silent.
Who needs more noise in the city?
Shameful waste. Heartbreaking litter.

feedback.es: Una palabra repetida, dos ideas opuestas, una pregunta sin respuesta y adjetivos cargados de emoción son las cuatro señales.

Old cars are noisy. New cars are silent.

prompt.es: Elige el efecto de la pregunta retórica del anuncio.

choices.text: It asks the reader to send an answer to the council.
It makes the reader feel that the answer is obvious.
It invites the reader to compare two different proposals.

feedback.es: La pregunta no espera respuesta: hace pensar al lector que la conclusión es obvia, y ese es su efecto.

origin.text: Why should we keep losing our green spaces to car parks, when every child needs somewhere safe to play?

prompt.es: Explica en una frase el efecto de la repetición del eslogan.

answer.text: The repetition of fresh makes the slogan easy to remember.
accepted: The repetition of fresh makes the slogan easy to remember.
The repetition of the word fresh makes the slogan memorable.
Repeating the word fresh makes the message easy to remember.
The repetition of fresh puts emphasis on the idea and makes it memorable.

feedback.es: El efecto de repetir una palabra es que el eslogan resulte fácil de recordar y refuerce la idea.

origin.text: Fresh food, fresh ideas, fresh start.

prompt.es: Escucha el pódcast y elige la técnica del cartel principal.

choices.text: A contrast between cheap trains and expensive cars.
Repetition of one word across several short phrases.
A rhetorical question that invites obvious agreement.

feedback.es: El cartel principal pregunta quién disfruta del tráfico: una pregunta retórica. La repetición de free pertenece a los carteles pequeños.

origin.audio: In this week's media podcast, a teacher examines a campaign that urges commuters to leave their cars at home. The main poster asks, Who enjoys sitting in traffic? Nobody answers, of course, because the audience already agrees. Smaller posters repeat the word free three times: free seats, free air, free time. The teacher admits that the campaign is memorable, yet she notes that it never mentions the cost of a train ticket.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué da a entender la profesora al final.

choices.text: That the campaign is memorable but leaves out a key fact.
That the campaign is weak and nobody will remember it.
That train tickets are cheaper than most people think.

feedback.es: Con yet señala un reparo: la campaña se recuerda, pero omite el precio del billete; no dice que fracase ni que sea barato.

Nobody answers, of course, because the audience already agrees. Smaller posters repeat the word free three times: free seats, free air, free time. The teacher admits that the campaign is memorable, yet she notes that it never mentions the cost of a train ticket.

prompt.es: Completa: «Su lenguaje es muy emotivo porque busca conmover, no dar datos.»

answer.text: emotive
accepted: emotive
emotional

feedback.es: Emotive describe el lenguaje que apela a los sentimientos en lugar de a los hechos.

origin.text: The poster uses words such as shameful and heartbreaking. Its language is highly ___ because it aims to move the reader's feelings rather than to provide facts.

prompt.es: Ordena: «La repetición ayuda a poner énfasis en la idea principal.»

answer.text: Repetition helps to put emphasis on the main idea

feedback.es: Put emphasis on + idea: así se nombra el efecto de destacar un mensaje.

prompt.es: Elige la técnica del eslogan de tres frases cortas.

choices.text: Contrast between children and empty parks.
Repetition of the same word to open each phrase.
A rhetorical question aimed at the parents.

feedback.es: Every abre cada frase corta: es repetición. La pregunta final es otra técnica distinta del eslogan de tres frases.

origin.text: Every child. Every park. Every day. This is the slogan of a playground campaign, which also asks parents: Would you want your child to grow up without a place to play?

prompt.es: Elige con qué propósito incluye el anuncio la pregunta sobre las dos horas.

choices.text: To ask readers how long their journey really takes.
To compare the price of bus and train tickets.
To make readers feel that driving wastes their time.

feedback.es: La pregunta no busca una cifra: quiere que el lector sienta que conducir es una pérdida de tiempo, y por eso es retórica.

origin.text: Switch to the bus, and you will have your mornings back. Why should anyone spend two hours a day in a queue of cars? The city has given you the choice; now make it.

prompt.es: Completa: «El autor quiere persuadir al lector de que use el autobús cada día.»

answer.text: persuade
accepted: persuade
convince

feedback.es: Persuade someone to + verbo: persuadir a alguien de que haga algo.

origin.text: The writer wants to ___ the reader to take the bus every day, so the advert uses feelings as well as facts.

es: Formar paralelismo, tricolon y antítesis con la misma estructura gramatical en cada parte, cuidar la simetría del ritmo y repasar el énfasis con so y such.

teaching.en: The speaker uses parallelism when every part of the sentence has the same grammar: we want to learn, to share and to grow.
teaching.es: El orador usa el paralelismo cuando cada parte de la frase tiene la misma gramática: queremos aprender, compartir y crecer.
teaching.explanationEs: Paralelismo: cada parte repite la misma forma (aquí, to + verbo).
segments: The speaker uses parallelism when every part of the sentence has the
same grammar: we want to learn, to share and to grow.
teaching.audioText: The speaker uses parallelism when every part of the sentence has the same grammar: we want to learn, to share and to grow.

teaching.en: A tricolon gives a sentence the rhythm of three, as in safe streets, clean air and happy people, and the third part usually lands with the most weight.
teaching.es: Un tricolon da a la frase el ritmo de tres, como en calles seguras, aire limpio y gente feliz, y la tercera parte suele caer con más peso.
teaching.explanationEs: Tricolon: tres partes seguidas con la misma forma; la última cierra con fuerza.
segments: A tricolon gives a sentence the rhythm of three, as in safe streets, clean
air and happy people, and the third part usually lands with the most weight.
teaching.audioText: A tricolon gives a sentence the rhythm of three, as in safe streets, clean air and happy people, and the third part usually lands with the most weight.

teaching.en: Antithesis places opposite ideas in the same structure, such as young in years but old in wisdom, so the contrast feels balanced and complete.
teaching.es: La antítesis coloca ideas opuestas en la misma estructura, como joven en años pero viejo en sabiduría, y así el contraste resulta equilibrado y completo.
teaching.explanationEs: Antítesis: opuestos (young/old) con estructura igual (adjetivo + in + nombre).
segments: Antithesis places opposite ideas in the same structure, such as young in
years but old in wisdom, so the contrast feels balanced and complete.
teaching.audioText: Antithesis places opposite ideas in the same structure, such as young in years but old in wisdom, so the contrast feels balanced and complete.

teaching.en: If one part changes its grammar, the symmetry breaks and the balance of the whole sentence is lost, so keep every part in the same form.
teaching.es: Si una parte cambia de gramática, la simetría se rompe y se pierde el equilibrio de toda la frase, así que mantén cada parte con la misma forma.
teaching.explanationEs: Simetría y equilibrio dependen de que las partes suenen igual.
segments: If one part changes its grammar, the symmetry breaks and the balance of
the whole sentence is lost, so keep every part in the same form.
teaching.audioText: If one part changes its grammar, the symmetry breaks and the balance of the whole sentence is lost, so keep every part in the same form.

teaching.en: An eloquent speaker often lets the final part grow longer or stronger, which helps to hammer home the main point.
teaching.es: Un orador elocuente suele dejar que la parte final sea más larga o más fuerte, lo que ayuda a machacar la idea principal.
teaching.explanationEs: Hammer home = dejar clara una idea a base de insistencia rítmica.
segments: An eloquent speaker often lets the final part grow longer
or stronger, which helps to hammer home the main point.
teaching.audioText: An eloquent speaker often lets the final part grow longer or stronger, which helps to hammer home the main point.

teaching.en: It was such a clear structure, and the speaker was so calm, that the speech felt persuasive and memorable in equal measure.
teaching.es: Era una estructura tan clara, y el orador estaba tan tranquilo, que el discurso resultó persuasivo y fácil de recordar en la misma medida.
teaching.explanationEs: Repaso: such + a + adjetivo + nombre + that; so + adjetivo + that.
segments: It was such a clear structure, and the speaker was so
calm, that the speech felt persuasive and memorable in equal measure.
teaching.audioText: It was such a clear structure, and the speaker was so calm, that the speech felt persuasive and memorable in equal measure.

prompt.es: Elige la versión con paralelismo: «Queremos aprender, compartir y crecer.»

choices.text: We want to learn, sharing and to grow.
We want to learn, to share and to grow.
We want learning, to share and growing.

feedback.es: Las tres partes usan to + verbo: esa igualdad de forma crea el paralelismo.

hint.es: Las tres partes deben tener la misma forma.

origin.text: A student drafts a line for the school council: she wants three verbs, each built in exactly the same way, to close her opening paragraph.

prompt.es: Completa la antítesis: «Es fácil empezar, pero difícil terminar.»

answer.text: hard
accepted: hard
difficult
tough

feedback.es: Hard (o difficult) se opone a easy y mantiene la estructura adjetivo + to + verbo.

origin.text: Her slogan is a perfect antithesis: it is easy to start, but ___ to finish. The opposite adjective keeps the same structure as the first part.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Queremos una escuela que escuche, aprenda y dirija.»

feedback.es: Tricolon: tres verbos en tercera persona con la misma forma (-s).

hint.es: Tres verbos seguidos con la misma terminación.

prompt.es: Une en un tricolon: limpiar, plantar y pintar.

accepted: We clean the park, plant trees and paint the benches.
We clean the park, we plant trees and we paint benches.
We clean the park, plant the trees and paint the benches.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con su técnica.

pairs: Less talk, more action.

feedback.es: Opuestos con la misma forma son antítesis; tres verbos seguidos son tricolon; dos partes iguales son paralelismo; such a + nombre da énfasis.

pairs: Less talk, more action.
We listen, we learn, we lead.

prompt.es: Elige cómo unir las dos frases con énfasis: «La voz era tan fuerte que todos escucharon.»

choices.text: The voice was such strong that everyone listened.
The voice was so a strong voice that everyone listened.
The voice was so strong that everyone listened.

feedback.es: Con un adjetivo solo se usa so + adjetivo + that; such exige un nombre: such a strong voice.

origin.text: At the school assembly, the speaker talked about litter for ten minutes. Her voice was strong, and nobody looked at their phones.

prompt.es: Escucha el discurso y elige qué contraste construye la oradora sobre los alumnos.

choices.text: A lot of talent but little time.
A lot of time but little talent.
A lot of rooms but few teachers.

feedback.es: Dice que los alumnos son ricos en talento pero pobres en tiempo: la antítesis rich in talent, poor in time.

origin.audio: Friends, this school has given us so much: it has taught us to think, to question and to care. Yet it has asked for so little in return. We are rich in talent, but poor in time; ready in spirit, but tired in body. Today I am not asking for something impossible. I am asking for one hour, one classroom and one chance to make our voices heard.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige con qué propósito pide solo «una hora».

choices.text: To admit that the students are not serious.
To make the request sound small and easy to accept.
To warn the school that the students will go on strike.

feedback.es: Tras decir que no pide algo imposible, enumera una hora, un aula y una oportunidad: presenta la petición como pequeña para que sea fácil aceptarla.

origin.audio: Friends, this school has given us so much: it has taught us to think, to question and to care. Yet it has asked for so little in return. feedback.es: Delante de a + adjetivo + nombre se usa such, no so.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué postura adopta la oradora ante el pasado.

choices.text: She admits it was hard but wants to move on.
She denies that there were any problems.
She blames the audience for the old arguments.

feedback.es: No niega el pasado, pero pide mirar más allá: reconoce la dificultad y propone avanzar.

origin.audio: Yesterday was difficult, but tomorrow will be brighter. Yesterday we were divided; tomorrow we will stand together. The speaker does not deny the past, yet she asks her audience to look beyond it.

es: Analizar un discurso breve, escrito y en audio: localizar la tesis, las técnicas (concesión, pregunta retórica, señalizadores), la apelación emocional y la llamada a la acción.

teaching.en: In the opening, the speaker states the thesis clearly, because a listener who hears a strong claim early can follow the rest of the argument.
teaching.es: En la apertura, el orador expone la tesis con claridad, porque un oyente que escucha pronto una afirmación sólida puede seguir el resto del argumento.
teaching.explanationEs: La tesis suele estar al principio; claim = afirmación que se defiende.
segments: In the opening, the speaker states the thesis clearly, because a listener who
hears a strong claim early can follow the rest of the argument.
teaching.audioText: In the opening, the speaker states the thesis clearly, because a listener who hears a strong claim early can follow the rest of the argument.

teaching.en: A speaker who can concede a point, for example by admitting that the plan is expensive, gains credibility with a sceptical audience.
teaching.es: Un orador que sabe admitir un punto, por ejemplo reconociendo que el plan es caro, gana credibilidad ante un público escéptico.
teaching.explanationEs: Concede a point: reconocer que el adversario tiene razón en algo; aumenta la credibilidad.
segments: A speaker who can concede a point, for example by admitting
that the plan is expensive, gains credibility with a sceptical audience.
teaching.audioText: A speaker who can concede a point, for example by admitting that the plan is expensive, gains credibility with a sceptical audience.

teaching.en: Phrases such as first, secondly and finally act as a signpost, helping listeners to see where the argument is going.
teaching.es: Expresiones como «primero», «en segundo lugar» y «por último» funcionan como señalizadores y ayudan al público a ver hacia dónde va el argumento.
teaching.explanationEs: Un signpost no añade información: guía al oyente por la estructura.
segments: Phrases such as first, secondly and finally act as a
signpost, helping listeners to see where the argument is going.
teaching.audioText: Phrases such as first, secondly and finally act as a signpost, helping listeners to see where the argument is going.

teaching.en: A rhetorical question is often used to appeal to the audience's feelings, which classical writers called pathos, rather than to logic.
teaching.es: Una pregunta retórica suele usarse para apelar a los sentimientos del público, lo que los autores clásicos llamaban pathos, más que a la lógica.
teaching.explanationEs: Appeal to + nombre: apelar a; pathos = apelación a la emoción.
segments: A rhetorical question is often used to appeal to the audience's
feelings, which classical writers called pathos, rather than to logic.
teaching.audioText: A rhetorical question is often used to appeal to the audience's feelings, which classical writers called pathos, rather than to logic.

teaching.en: The closing usually ends with a call to action, such as sign the petition tonight, and this is how a speaker tries to rally support.
teaching.es: El cierre suele terminar con una llamada a la acción, como «firma la petición esta noche», y así intenta el orador reunir apoyos.
teaching.explanationEs: La llamada a la acción pide algo concreto: quién, qué y cuándo.
segments: The closing usually ends with a call to action, such as sign the
petition tonight, and this is how a speaker tries to rally support.
teaching.audioText: The closing usually ends with a call to action, such as sign the petition tonight, and this is how a speaker tries to rally support.

teaching.en: To summarise, the speaker argues that the school needs a garden, uses a tricolon to build the claim and asks the audience to sign the petition.
teaching.es: En resumen, la oradora sostiene que el colegio necesita un huerto, usa un tricolon para construir la afirmación y pide al público que firme la petición.
teaching.explanationEs: Resumen: argues that + tesis; asks the audience to + acción.
segments: To summarise, the speaker argues that the school needs a garden, uses a
tricolon to build the claim and asks the audience to sign the petition.
teaching.audioText: To summarise, the speaker argues that the school needs a garden, uses a tricolon to build the claim and asks the audience to sign the petition.

origin.audio: Good morning, everyone. Every day, three hundred students walk along a road without a pavement. Some of you may say that a path is expensive, and I accept that it is. First, though, think of the risk. Secondly, think of the cost of doing nothing. Finally, ask yourself this: would you let your own child cross that road? Today I will argue that our school needs a safe path, and I ask you to support it.
